Method of Attack: Encrypts files using AES encryption with a unique key per file
Purposely deletes backups by overwriting backup files multiple times before deletion
Deletes shadow volume copies, disables startup repair, clears event logs
Terminates processes related to backup and system management (sql, taskmgr, regedit, backup)
Renames encrypted files to format Zenis-[2 random chars].[12 random chars]
Creates ransom notes (Zenis-Instructions.html) with instructions and embedded encrypted data
Uses a hidden base64 encoded string in ransom note decryptable only by private RSA key
Checks for execution filename and registry key to decide whether to encrypt
Impacted Systems: Windows systems with Remote Desktop services potentially hacked
Attack Vector: Likely via hacked Remote Desktop services
Indicators of Compromise: Emails in ransom note: TheZenis@Tutanota.com, TheZenis@MailFence.com, TheZenis@Protonmail.com, TheZenis@Mail2Tor.com
